overview: 15146 Moorpark St is a seven unit apartment building in the heart of Sherman Oaks, built in 2005 and delivered on a certificate of occupancy issued 23 February 2007. The units are two story townhomes, six two-bedroom and one three-bedroom, laid out across 10,780 building square feet on a 7,804 square foot lot, over a gated subterranean garage. Every unit has its own washer and dryer, a fireplace, central heat and air, a private balcony, and its own gas and electric meter. Tenants share a roof deck with a view across Ventura Boulevard.

The certificate of occupancy date is what separates this building from most of what trades in the Valley. The Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance reaches buildings occupied before 1 October 1978, and ZIMAS returns RSO: No for this parcel. Annual increases follow AB 1482, the state Tenant Protection Act, at 5% plus regional CPI to a 10% ceiling, and turnover resets to market.

Six of the seven units are occupied on month to month tenancies at $2,975 to $3,575. The seventh is vacant and delivers empty. Ownership's own 2026 statements show a landlord cost structure limited to water, common-area power, refuse, insurance and routine service, because every unit is separately metered and every unit does its own laundry.
properties.location_title: One Block North of Ventura Boulevard in Sherman Oaks
location_narrative: The property sits on Moorpark Street one block north of Ventura Boulevard, roughly a tenth of a mile from the Sherman Oaks Galleria at 15301 Ventura Blvd and a short walk from Whole Foods, Trader Joe's and Westfield Fashion Square. ZIMAS places the parcel inside a Transit Priority Area, within a half mile of a major transit stop under AB 2097, in Transit Oriented Communities Tier 3, and in the state's highest resource tier for opportunity. The 101 is four minutes north and the 405 four minutes west.

The largest thing happening to this location is not on the block. On 22 January 2026 the Metro Board selected the Locally Preferred Alternative for the Sepulveda Transit Corridor, a fully underground heavy rail line running from the Van Nuys Metrolink station under the Santa Monica Mountains to the Westside, with a Ventura Boulevard station in Sherman Oaks. Metro estimates a 20 minute one seat ride from the Valley to UCLA and Westwood on a route that today takes an hour in traffic. The project carries a $24.2B budget and the initial operating segment is targeted for 2033 to 2035. It is in environmental review, not under construction, so nothing in this valuation assumes it. A Sherman Oaks rental one block from the boulevard that station will sit on is nonetheless a different asset in 2035 than it is today.

The retail around it is turning over in the buyer's favor. Hapa Haus is taking 7,983 square feet at the Sherman Oaks Galleria, with 69 indoor seats, a covered patio and five golf simulators, targeting a November 2026 opening. Yama Sushi Marketplace is building out roughly 7,200 square feet at 15300 Ventura Blvd. Burger She Wrote opened its second location at 14245 Ventura Blvd in March 2026, and Aromas Indian Cuisine is taking the former Billa space at 14350 Ventura Blvd. All four sit within about half a mile of the property.

New housing is arriving too, and most of it is the kind that sets a rent ceiling rather than competing for this tenant. Via Avanti at 4827 N Sepulveda Blvd is a 325 unit mixed-use complex with ground-floor retail near the Galleria that finished wrapping at the end of 2025. The former Sunkist headquarters at 14130 Riverside Drive, a Brutalist landmark, is being converted into 95 apartments. A 75 unit affordable building is proposed at 14318 W Dickens St, one block south of Ventura. New institutional product asks institutional rents, and a 2005 townhome with its own washer and dryer and a private garage space rents at a discount to it without feeling like one.

Matthews reported in January 2026 that Sherman Oaks RSO pricing held flat per unit through 2025 while cap rates expanded and gross rent multipliers compressed, and that the gap between RSO and AB 1482 assets is expected to widen. That is the whole thesis for this building in one sentence. Buyers are paying up for predictable rent growth and a clean operating story, and they are discounting everything that comes with a rent board.
physical_narrative: LADBS records the original permit as a new two story, seven unit Type V apartment building over a Type I basement parking garage, with the certificate of occupancy issued 23 February 2007. Permits finaled in 2006 cover seven central heating and air conditioning systems, fireplaces in all seven units, a fire sprinkler system for the building and garage, corridor ventilation, and individual electrical meters and panels for each apartment. A seismic gas shutoff valve is recorded as installed.

The assessor carries 10,780 building square feet, 15 bedrooms and a D6 quality class on a 7,804 square foot lot zoned [Q]R3-1. The public rental listings for the building describe units of 987 to 1,275 square feet, granite counters, high ceilings, in-unit washers and dryers, private balconies, secure gated parking and a roof deck available to all tenants. Per-unit square footage in this analysis is allocated across the assessor's total rather than measured.

Interiors in the current listing photography show renovated kitchens with shaker cabinetry, granite counters and stainless appliances, wide plank flooring throughout, updated baths with tiled showers, and stacked washer and dryer units inside each home. The 2019 sale photography for the same building shows the original maple cabinetry and tile, so the work is recent.

The capital a buyer inherits sits in the permit record rather than in a deferred list. Seven individual central heating and air conditioning systems, seven fireplaces, a fire sprinkler system covering both the building and the garage, corridor ventilation, individual electrical meters and panels in every apartment, and a seismic gas shutoff valve all carry finaled LADBS permits. LADBS records no code enforcement case on the parcel. The interior renovation since then is cosmetic work of a kind that does not require a permit, which is why it does not appear in the record.
market_narrative: The buyer for this building is not buying a repositioning. Rents are already at or near the top of the Sherman Oaks range for this unit type, the interiors are done, and the capital items a buyer normally holds money back for are behind it. What they are buying is a rule set: a Los Angeles apartment building where the annual increase is a published formula, turnover resets to market, and the operating statement has five lines on it.

That pool is smaller than the pool for a twenty unit RSO building and it moves faster. The competing Sherman Oaks listing, five townhomes on Stern Avenue, is asking $639,000 a unit and has been out 41 days, which tells us where the ceiling is and roughly how long it takes to find out.

Days on market across the three closed sales: 17 days on 13430 Victory Blvd, which closed 1.7% above its ask; 13 days on 10833-10835 Camarillo St, which closed 9.2% below its ask; and zero on 4609 Kester Ave, which never reached the MLS as a listing and traded off market. The four active listings carried here have been out 41, 72, 147 and 248 days, and the two that have sat longest are the two asking the most per unit.
positioning_narrative: We position the building on what a buyer owns on day one rather than on what they could do to it. Seven large townhome units in prime Sherman Oaks, one delivered vacant, in-unit laundry and a private garage space behind a gate, no rent board, and a landlord expense load limited to water, power in the common areas and refuse. The rent upside is real but modest, and we would rather be believed on a 5% number than doubted on a 20% one.
rent_narrative: Seven Sherman Oaks comparables, four two-bedroom and three three-bedroom, pulled on 16 September 2026. Every one is an asking rent rather than a signed lease, and they are presented as a market sensitivity rather than as achieved rents. The two-bedroom rows ask $2,995 to $3,295 and average $3,171. The three-bedroom rows ask $3,450 to $3,995 and average $3,813.

The two comparables closest to the subject on unit size are 15210 Ventura Blvd at 1,257 square feet asking $3,295, eight hundredths of a mile away, and 14934 Burbank Blvd at 1,200 square feet asking $3,195. The subject's two-bedroom townhomes are in place at $2,975 to $2,995, below both. Market rent is carried at $3,195 a unit, which is the Burbank Blvd ask and sits $100 under the nearest and best matched comparable in the set.

The three-bedroom is in place at $3,575 against a comparable range of $3,450 to $3,995. Market rent is carried at $3,650, a step above the rent in place and well inside the comparable range. The 4325 Stern Avenue listing a mile and a half east, five three-bedroom townhomes built in 2008, carries in-place rents of $3,300 to $3,750 on units a little smaller than this one.

This is not a repositioning story and we are not going to present it as one. The building is already collecting most of what its submarket pays. The evidence supports a step up on turnover, 5.3% across the rent roll, and it does not support more than that.
valuation_narrative: The suggested list price of $3,125,000 is $446,429 a unit and $289.89 per square foot. Against the three closed sales it sits just under the $450,000 a unit 4609 Kester Ave paid a third of a mile west, and 29% under the $408.67 per square foot median of the set. Those two readings come from the same fact: at 1,540 gross square feet a unit the subject carries 40% more space per unit than Kester and nearly twice Camarillo St, so it earns the unit price and gives back the foot price.

On $157,228 of current net operating income the price is a 5.03% capitalization rate, and 5.44% once market rents are in place. That sits above 4609 Kester Ave at 4.80% and 13430 Victory Blvd at 4.79%, and below 10833-10835 Camarillo St at 5.93%, each struck on that transaction's own recorded net operating income. The gross rent multiplier of 12.02 lands between Camarillo at 11.47 and Victory at 13.85.

The operating statement carries ownership's own 2026 refuse, water and power, repairs and grounds figures, with three lines a buyer adds that the current owner does not pay in the same form: property taxes reassessed to the sale price, a 5% management fee, and a replacement reserve. Operating expenses run 37.7% of effective gross income, which is where a seven unit building sits when every unit is separately metered, every unit does its own laundry, and there is no elevator, no pool and no on-site staff.

Every metric lands inside the comparable set rather than reaching past it, which is what gets an offer in the first three weeks instead of the third month. The two marketed comparables traded in 17 and 13 days. The only competing Sherman Oaks offering of this product is asking $639,000 a unit and has been out 41 days without trading.

buyer_profiles.copy: A Valley family or partnership that already owns within a few miles and wants a seven unit building they can operate themselves. Kester Ave, a third of a mile west, traded off market to exactly this kind of buyer.

The subject sits on one APN today, and no subdivision is assumed anywhere in this valuation.
